title: MyLens
summary: 1-1 Live Presentations at Scale with AI.
body: MyLens is AI for live 1-1 presentations at scale. You add your raw sources, say what matters, and invite your audience. MyLens AI gives every person a live, private presentation, answers their questions using your sources, and create new slides and layers in real time during the presentation. Then the AI tells you how each session went, so you can see who’s doing well, who’s stuck, and what to do next.

title: Bee Frontier and Bee Eclipse
summary: Amazon's personal AI memory, now on your wrist or phone
body: Bee Frontier and Bee Eclipse are Amazon's new personal AI devices that help you remember what matters. Frontier is a wearable for your wrist or clothing, while Eclipse attaches magnetically to your phone. Both capture conversations and turn them into useful summaries, reminders, and follow-ups without retaining audio recordings. With Alexa+ integration, your personal AI memory can help you recall important details and act on them later.

title: Openbroca
summary: Lightweight AI dictation for Mac that sounds like you
body: Openbroca is a native Swift AI dictation app for Mac, with a ~6.5 MB download. Press a shortcut, speak naturally, and get clean text right where you're typing. It removes fillers and repetition while keeping your meaning and tone, with no prompt tweaking. Includes a personal dictionary that learns from corrections, Typeless dictionary import, and translation into 28 languages. All features are free to try.

Release: llm-echo 0.5

I'm working towards a new LLM release, and testing PRs caused me to revisit the llm-echo debug plugin. This plugin provides a "model" which doesn't involve an LLM at all - it just repeats back the prompts that have been fed to it. The new release now updates the simulated token usage counts to take tool calls, system prompts, and reasoning tokens into account.

Example usage:

uvx --with llm-echo llm -m echo 'hi there' -o thinking 1 --usage
